hero.title: RICHTER
hero.subtitle: Sound design for a short film. Everything recorded from scratch—no libraries. Basic recording gear only.

overview.title: What I Did
overview.desc: Recorded and designed all sound for Richter. No libraries—everything came from field recordings (Zoom H6), synths (Vital, ReaSynth, TAL Noisemaker), and manual foley. Student budget, so I had to be creative with basic gear.
overview.field_desc: Recorded ambiences, room tones, and textures with a Zoom H6. Every sound in the film is an original recording—no library samples.
overview.synth_desc: Built drones and risers in Vital, ReaSynth, and TAL Noisemaker. The alarm sound is pure synthesis—no samples.
overview.foley_desc: Recorded footsteps on wood, concrete, and carpet. Door sounds. Paper handling. Cloth movement. Layered and processed in Cubase to match the picture.
overview.mix_desc: Balanced dialogue, SFX, and ambience. Automated volume and EQ to follow the story. Mixed in Reaper.

technical.title: How I Made It
technical.desc: Mixed in Reaper. Zoom H6 for field recording. Used granular stretching in Cubase for tension textures. Wrote a short orchestral score—strings and brass—timed to scene cuts.

block1.title: How I Made It
block1.content: Recorded footsteps on wood, concrete, carpet. Door sounds. Paper handling. Cloth movement. Processed in Cubase with granular stretching for tension textures. Wrote a short orchestral score—strings and brass—timed to scene cuts.
